urgency_label: Monitor closely. Contact your vet for guidance.
assessment: Two squares of dark chocolate for a 30kg dog is a low-to-moderate dose of theobromine. At this weight, serious toxicity usually requires a larger amount, but dark chocolate has a higher theobromine concentration than milk chocolate. Your dog will likely be fine, but monitoring is important.
immediate_actions: Do not induce vomiting unless your vet specifically instructs you to
Note the exact time of ingestion and type of chocolate
Call your vet or poison helpline for specific guidance based on the chocolate brand
Keep your dog in a calm environment and ensure access to water
watch_for: Vomiting or diarrhea in the next 2-4 hours
Rapid breathing or elevated heart rate
Muscle tremors or seizures (rare at this dose but seek emergency care immediately)
vet_questions: Exactly how much chocolate and what brand/type?
What is your dog's exact weight?
How long ago did ingestion occur?
timeframe: Monitor for the next 6-12 hours. If any symptoms from the watch list appear, go to emergency vet immediately.
voice_summary: OK, don't panic. Two squares of dark chocolate for a 30 kilo lab is on the lower end of concerning. Your dog will probably be fine, but I want you to call your vet now and give them the details. Watch for vomiting, restlessness, or rapid breathing over the next few hours. If you see any of those, head to the emergency vet right away.
